parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State what is meant by a photon.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead: A laser emits red light of a single wavelength. The light is produced when electrons move from a higher energy level to a lower energy level. The difference in energy between the two levels is 1.96 eV.
parts.text: Calculate the wavelength of the light.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
The power of the beam emitted by the laser is 1.0 × 10⁻² W.

Calculate the number of photons emitted per unit time by the laser.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
The photons are incident normal to a surface. Half of the number of photons are absorbed by the surface, and half are reflected.

Determine the average force exerted by the beam of photons on the surface.
